name: root
description: The head of the whole sentence. Exactly one token per sentence; its head is left empty (shown as 0).

name: nominal subject
description: A nominal that is the syntactic subject of a clause. 'The DOG barked.'

name: object
description: The direct object — the second core argument of a transitive verb. 'She read the BOOK.'

name: indirect object
description: A core argument other than subject or direct object, typically a recipient. 'She gave ME the book.'

name: clausal subject
description: A clause functioning as the subject. 'WHAT SHE SAID matters.'

name: clausal complement
description: A clausal object with its own subject. 'He says THAT YOU LIKE IT.'

name: open clausal complement
description: A predicative complement whose subject is supplied from outside. 'She tried TO LEAVE.'

name: oblique nominal
description: A non-core nominal, usually adverbial — place, time, manner. 'He slept IN THE GARDEN.'

name: vocative
description: A nominal used to address someone. 'MARY, come here.'

name: expletive
description: A semantically empty placeholder in subject position. 'THERE is a problem.'

name: dislocated element
description: A fronted or trailing element outside the normal argument structure. 'The book, I READ IT yesterday.'

name: adverbial clause modifier
description: A clause modifying a predicate — time, condition, purpose, cause. 'IF IT RAINS, we stay.'

name: adverbial modifier
description: An adverb or adverbial phrase modifying a predicate or modifier. 'She sang QUIETLY.'

name: discourse element
description: Interjections, fillers, and discourse particles. 'WELL, I think so.'

name: auxiliary
description: A function word marking tense, aspect, mood, voice or polarity. 'She HAS left.'

name: copula
description: A linking verb joining a subject to a non-verbal predicate. 'She IS a teacher.'

name: marker
description: A word introducing a subordinate clause. 'I know THAT he left.'

name: nominal modifier
description: A nominal modifying another nominal, often possessive or prepositional. 'the roof OF THE HOUSE'

name: appositional modifier
description: A nominal that renames or elaborates another nominal. 'Sam, MY BROTHER, called.'

name: numeric modifier
description: A numeral modifying a nominal. 'THREE books'

name: clausal modifier of noun
description: A clause modifying a nominal, including relative clauses. 'the man WHO LEFT'

name: adjectival modifier
description: An adjective modifying a nominal. 'the OLD dog'

name: determiner
description: An article, demonstrative or quantifier specifying a nominal. 'THE dog'

name: classifier
description: A numeral classifier accompanying a counted nominal. Common in East and Southeast Asian languages.

name: case marking
description: An adposition or case affix attaching to a nominal. 'in THE garden' — 'in' attaches to 'garden'.

name: conjunct
description: A non-first element of a coordination, attached to the first conjunct. 'tea and COFFEE'

name: coordinating conjunction
description: The coordinator itself, attached to the following conjunct. 'tea AND coffee'

name: fixed multiword
description: A grammaticalised fixed expression treated as one unit. 'as WELL as'

name: flat multiword
description: A headless multiword unit such as a personal name or date. 'Anna KARENINA'

name: compound
description: A noun or verb compound. 'PHONE book'

name: list
description: Comparable items in a list, such as contact details in a signature block.

name: parataxis
description: Clauses joined without a coordinator or subordinator. 'He said it — I HEARD him.'

name: orphan
description: Links surviving dependents when their head has been elided in gapping.

name: goes with
description: Joins parts of a word wrongly split in the original text.

name: reparandum
description: A disfluency that the speaker repairs. 'Go to the righ— TO THE LEFT.'

name: punctuation
description: A punctuation mark, attached to the head of the phrase it delimits.

name: unspecified dependency
description: Fallback when the relation cannot be determined or no other label fits.
